title: Investigate host-staging alignment leaks during hybrid continuous batching
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Observed gradual GPU RSS growth and host pinned memory spikes when serving mixed workload profiles (short chat turns + occasional long generation) under the continuous batching runtime with cudaMallocAsync. The suspected root cause is misaligned host-staging span reuse combined with the pooling layer’s sub-allocation strategy causing tombstoned spans that prevent cudaMallocAsync from returning pages to the OS. This ticket captures reproducer, investigation notes, and proposed mitigations.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Sofia: Nightly cluster traces showed 18% RSS growth over 24h on canary with hybrid traffic (10% long requests). Snapshots attached. Initial hypothesis: host staging slab fragmentation + slow stream free -> cudaMallocAsync retention.

2026-02-23 - Arjun: Built repro microbenchmark that alternates sequences of 8-32 tokens (fast) and 2048 tokens (long). Reproducer reproduces leak within ~6k requests. Microbenchmark: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-host-staging/tree/ENG-812345 (link internal).

2026-02-25 - Arjun: Heap profiler dump (nsys + memtracker) shows pinned host staging allocations not freed on async free path when batch merges cross stream boundaries. Suspect: staging slab uses 64KB spans but long requests request odd sizes leading to misaligned suballocations and stale free-list pointers.

2026-02-28 - Sofia: Correlated KV cache warmup traces: cache warmup for long requests pins KV slices on device which prevents eviction; combined with host staging misalignments, page residency persists even after logical free. Customer-visible symptom: slow memory growth, occasional OOMs for heavy mixed tenants.

2026-03-02 - Eng review: Spike repro demo during standup. Decided to add detailed allocation tagging in the runtime (alloc origin: "host-staging-suballoc", request_id, stream_id, batch_id) and to add a stress test to CI that mimics mixed-seqlen traffic patterns.

2026-03-05 - Arjun: PR opened with additional allocation tags and a streaming sync fence before cudaFreeAsync for suspected edge-case where stream completes but host staging pointer still referenced by merged batch. PR: GH#7482 (internal).

2026-03-07 - QA: Ran long burn on canary with tagged allocs. Observed that leak rate reduced but not eliminated. Deeper issue: pooling's span-splitting algorithm produces leftover tiny fragments that remain in "pending-free" list because the async free callback orders differ when batches merge across streams.

2026-03-10 - Arjun: Proposed two-phase mitigation: (1) conservative span coalescing at pool free time (eager coalesce of adjacent free subspans belonging to same slab), (2) fallback synchronous decommit for spans older than X seconds to force cudaMallocAsync return. Plan: A/B test on canary next week.

Next steps: schedule PR to add coalescing + age-based synchronous decommit; add CI stress test; follow-up investigation on KV cache and eviction timing (possible race between device eviction and host free).
